paragraphs: Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. is principally engaged in the operation and development of the Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® concept ("Cracker Barrel"). Originally founded in 1969, we are headquartered in Lebanon, Tennessee and are organized under the laws of the State of Tennessee.

We maintain a website at crackerbarrel.com. We make available free of charge through our website our periodic and other reports filed with or furnished to the SEC pursuant to the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the "Exchange Act"), as soon as reasonably practicable after we file such material with, or furnish it to, the SEC. Information on our website is not deemed to be incorporated by reference into this Annual Report on Form 10-K or any other filings that we make from time to time with the SEC.

As of September 12, 2025, we operated 657 Cracker Barrel stores in 43 states and 68 Maple Street Biscuit Company stores in 10 states. The following description of our business should be read in conjunction with the information in Part II of this report under the caption "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and "Item 8. Financial Statements and Supplementary Data."

Our Cracker Barrel stores are intended to appeal to both the traveler and the local customer, and we believe they have consistently been a consumer favorite. We pride ourselves on our consistent quality, value and friendly service. As of September 12, 2025, no Cracker Barrel stores were franchised.

In 2024, we announced our multi-year strategic plan. The multi-year strategic plan is anchored on three overarching business imperatives: driving relevancy, delivering food and an experience guests love, and growing profitability. We have undertaken certain initiatives as part of these imperatives, including modifying capital allocation to support increased investment in the business to drive organic growth.

Store Format: The format of our stores consists of a trademarked rustic old country-store design offering a full-service restaurant menu that features home-style country food and a wide variety of decorative and functional items such as rocking chairs, holiday and seasonal gifts, toys, apparel, cookware and foods. All stores are freestanding buildings and consist of approximately 20% of gift shop space with the remainder dedicated to our restaurant, training and storage space. Our stores have stone fireplaces and are decorated with antique‑style furnishings and other authentic and nostalgic items, reminiscent of and similar to those found and sold in the past in traditional old country stores. The front porch of each store features rows of the signature Cracker Barrel rocking chairs, which are a popular item sold by the gift shops and which we invite guests to use while waiting for a table in our dining room or after enjoying a meal.

Products: Our restaurants, which generated approximately 81% of our total revenue in 2025, offer home-style country cooking featuring many of our own recipes that emphasize authenticity and quality. Our restaurants serve breakfast, lunch and dinner daily and offer dine-in, pick-up and delivery services. Menu items are moderately priced. Approximately 93% of our restaurants also serve an assortment of beer and wine.

Breakfast items can be ordered at any time throughout the day and include juices, eggs, pancakes, meats, grits, and a variety of biscuit specialties, such as gravy and biscuits and country ham and biscuits. Lunch and dinner items include fried and grilled chicken, chicken and dumplings, meatloaf, country fried steak, pork chops, fish, country fried shrimp, steak, vegetable plates, sandwiches and salads. We also offer multi-serving takeout family meal baskets. Additionally, from time to time, we feature new items as off-menu specials or on test menus at certain locations to evaluate possible ways to enhance customer interest and identify potential future additions to the menu. We offer weekday lunch specials, which include some of our favorite entrées in lunch-sized portions. Our menu also features weekday and weekend dinner specials that showcase a popular dinner entrée. There is some variation in menu pricing and content in different regions of the country. The average check per guest during 2025 was $15.23, which represents a 6.8% increase over the prior year. We served an average of approximately 5,330 restaurant guests per week in a typical store in 2025.

Our gift shops feature a variety of items inspired by our restaurant menu, such as pies, cornbread mix, coffee, syrups and pancake mix, as well as a broad selection of decorative and functional items, including rocking chairs, seasonal gifts, apparel, toys, cookware and various other gift items. We also offer an assortment of candies, preserves and other food items.

headings: Risks Related to Macroeconomic and Industry Conditions

Purchase price volatility and inflationary conditions may adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial performance, and measures we take to offset or mitigate such conditions may not be effective.
Risks Related to Our Business
Failure to achieve the goals or sustain the results of our multi-year strategic plan may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
We face intense competition, and if we are unable to continue to compete effectively, our business, financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected.
Failure to maximize or to successfully assert our intellectual property rights could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Risks Related to our Capital Structure
Provisions in the indentures governing the 2026 Notes or the 2030 Notes could delay or discourage a takeover of us.
The capped call transactions in connection with the 2030 Notes may affect the value of our common stock.
The convertible note hedge and warrant transactions in connection with the 2026 Notes may affect the value of our common stock.
We are subject to counterparty risk with respect to the convertible note hedge transactions and capped call transactions.
Risks Related to Supply Chains

Our reliance on certain significant vendors, particularly for foreign-sourced retail products, subjects us to risks, which may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Our ability to manage our retail inventory levels and changes in merchandise mix may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.
Risks Related to IT Systems, Cybersecurity and Data Privacy
A material disruption in our information technology, network infrastructure and telecommunication systems could have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

If we fail or our vendors fail to comply with privacy and data protection laws or our systems are compromised, our operations could be negatively impacted and we could be subject to litigation and adverse publicity.
Legal and Regulatory Risks
Litigation may adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
Our business could be negatively affected as a result of actions of activist shareholders.
Provisions in our charter, Tennessee law and our shareholder rights agreement may discourage potential acquirers of the Company.
Risks Related to Our Business Strategy
We are dependent upon attracting and retaining qualified employees while also controlling labor costs.
The loss of key executives or difficulties in recruiting and retaining qualified personnel could jeopardize our future growth and success.
We may pursue strategic investments or initiatives now or in the future, which may not yield their expected benefits, resulting in a loss of some or all of our investment.
Individual store locations are affected by local conditions that could change and adversely affect the carrying value of those locations.
Failure to adequately address sustainability matters could adversely affect our brand, business, results of operations and financial condition.
If we fail to execute our business strategy, which includes our ability to find new store locations and open new stores that are profitable, our business could suffer.
paragraphs: Investing in our securities involves a degree of risk. Persons buying our securities should carefully consider the risks described below and the other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K and other filings that we make from time to time with the SEC, including our consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes. If any of the following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition, results of operations or cash flows could be materially adversely affected. In any such case, the trading price of our securities could decline and you could lose all or part of your investment.

The strength of our revenues and results of operations are dependent upon, among other things, the price and availability of food, ingredients, retail merchandise, transportation, distribution, labor and utilities. We have experienced and continue to experience inflationary pressures with respect to these costs. Fluctuations in economic conditions, weather, supply chain disruptions, freight efficiency, demand and other factors also affect the availability, quality and cost of the ingredients and retail merchandise that we buy. Changes in global demand for corn, wheat and dairy products have caused and could continue to cause volatility in the feed costs for poultry and livestock. Operating margins for our restaurants are subject to changes in the price and availability of food commodities, including beef, pork, chicken, dairy and produce. The effect of, introduction of, or changes to tariffs or exchange rates on imported retail products or food products could increase our costs and possibly affect the supply of those products. Changes in demand for over-the-road transportation and distribution services could cause volatility, increase our costs and adversely affect our operating margins.

In addition, the prices of our retail merchandise are similarly impacted by economic and inflationary pressures, which have caused and may continue to cause higher costs and lower margins. Our attempts to offset cost pressures, such as through menu price increases and operational improvements, may not be successful. We seek to provide a moderately priced product, and, as a result, we may not seek to or be able to pass along price increases to our customers sufficient to completely offset cost increases without adversely affecting our customers' demand. Consumers may be less willing to pay our menu prices and may increasingly visit lower-priced competitors or may limit their restaurant or retail purchases. The extent to which price increases are not sufficient to offset higher costs adequately or in a timely manner, and/or result in significant decreases in revenue volume, may have a material adverse effect on our revenues and results of operations.

Labor is a primary component in our operating costs, and increases in labor costs due to increased minimum wages, competition, unemployment rates, or health care and other benefit costs may have a material adverse effect on our results of operations. We operate in many states and localities where the minimum wage is significantly higher than the federal minimum wage. Our distributors and suppliers could also be affected by higher minimum wage, benefit standards and compliance costs, which could result in higher costs for goods and services supplied to us. The market for labor in the United States is competitive, which has resulted in upward pressure on wages and may continue to do so in the future.

Our operating margins are also affected, whether as a result of general inflation or otherwise, by fluctuations in the price of utilities such as natural gas and electricity, on which our locations depend for much of their energy supply. Our failure to anticipate and respond effectively to one or more adverse changes in any of these factors could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations. Inflationary pressures and other fluctuations impacting the cost of these items could have a negative impact on our business in 2026.

Pandemics, epidemics, endemics, and other public health concerns, or government regulation relating to the consumption of food products and widespread infectious diseases could reduce consumer traffic and may have an adverse effect on our business, results of operations and financial condition.

Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. (the "Company," "our" or "we") is a publicly traded (Nasdaq: CBRL) company that, through its operations and those of certain subsidiaries, is principally engaged in the operation and development of the Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® ("Cracker Barrel") concept. Each Cracker Barrel store consists of a restaurant with a gift shop. The restaurants serve breakfast, lunch and dinner. The gift shop offers a variety of decorative and functional items specializing in rocking chairs, holiday gifts, toys, apparel and foods. As of September 12, 2025, the Company operated 657 Cracker Barrel stores located in 43 states. The Company also owns Maple Street Biscuit Company ("MSBC"), a breakfast and lunch fast casual concept. As of September 12, 2025, the Company operated 68 MSBC locations in ten states.

Management believes that the Cracker Barrel brand remains one of the strongest and most differentiated brands in the restaurant industry, and we plan to continue to leverage and build on that strength as a core competitive component of our business strategy. Our long-term strategy is anchored on three overarching business imperatives: driving relevancy, delivering food and experiences guests love, and growing profitability.

We believe there are significant challenges in the macroeconomic outlook for the coming quarters, including continued volatility of inflation and interest rates, higher consumer debt levels and lower savings rates, as well as the potential uncertainty associated with the geopolitical environment and global trade among other factors. However, despite these challenges, we remain focused on delivering long-term growth and returns for shareholders.
In 2024, we announced our multi-year strategic plan. The multi-year strategic plan is built on five pillars which have progressed over 2025. The five pillars are as follows:

● Refining the brand: We established an updated brand identity anchored on "the goodness of country hospitality", which has been applied in our marketing, products (food and retail) and physical content and assets. We have also refined our partnership strategy – partnering with NASCAR, for example – and expanded our use of additional marketing channels.

● Evolving the store and guest experience: We improved several operational speed metrics and implemented a new allocation software package to improve retail product management. Additionally, numerous retail floor layouts and store remodel packages were tested to enhance guests' browsing and shopping experience. The Remodel Program has been suspended based on guest feedback gathered through this testing.

● Winning in digital and off-premise: We further leveraged our loyalty program by employing advanced technologies to deliver offers tailored to individual guests and optimized and expanded our off-premise business by updating our holiday and catering programs and improving our third-party sales strategies.
Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc. 主要從事 Cracker Barrel Old Country Store® 概念（"Cracker Barrel"）的經營與發展。原於 1969 年創立，本公司總部設於田納西州的 Lebanon，並依據田納西州法律設立。
本公司網站為 crackerbarrel.com。我們透過網站提供免費取得本公司依證券交易法 1934 年版（"Exchange Act"）及其修正案，向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交或提供之定期及其他報告，於合理可行之時限內，於提交或提供該等資料後立即提供。本公司網站之資訊不被視為已納入本 10-K 年度報告或本公司不時向 SEC 提交之其他申報文件。
截至 2025 年 9 月 12 日，本公司經營 43 個州的 657 家 Cracker Barrel 店鋪，以及 10 個州的 68 家 Maple Street Biscuit Company 店鋪。以下本公司業務之描述應與本報告第二部分之內容配合閱讀，內容為 "項目 7. 管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之分析" 及 "項目 8. 財務報表與補充資料"。
本公司 Cracker Barrel 店鋪旨在吸引旅客與當地顧客，我們相信這些店鋪一直深受消費者喜愛。我們以持續的品質、價值與親切服務為傲。截至 2025 年 9 月 12 日，尚無 Cracker Barrel 店鋪為加盟模式。
2024 年，本公司宣佈了我們的多年戰略計畫。該多年戰略計畫以三大核心業務目標為基礎：提升相關性、提供顧客喜愛的餐點與體驗，以及提高獲利能力。我們已針對這些目標進行若干計畫，包括調整資本配置以支持增加對業務的投資，以推動內生性成長。

店鋪格式：本公司店鋪的設計為註冊商標的鄉村老商店風格，提供全服務餐廳菜單，特色為家常風味的鄉村餐點，以及廣泛的裝飾與實用商品，如搖椅、節日與季節禮品、玩具、服飾、炊具與食品。所有店鋪皆為獨立建築，約 20% 空間為禮品店，其餘為餐廳、訓練與儲存空間。本公司店鋪設有石頭壁爐，並以古董風格傢俱及其他真實且懷舊的物品裝飾，與過去傳統鄉村商店中所見與銷售的商品相似。每家店鋪的前門廊設有數排標誌性的 Cracker Barrel 搖椅，這些搖椅為禮品店熱銷商品，我們歡迎顧客在用餐前於餐廳等候區或用餐後使用。
產品：本公司餐廳在 2025 年產生約 81% 的總營業收入，提供家常風味的鄉村餐點，包含許多本公司自製食譜，強調真實性與品質。本公司餐廳每日提供早餐、午餐與晚餐，並提供內用、外帶與送餐服務。餐點價格中等。約 93% 的餐廳同時提供啤酒與葡萄酒。

早餐項目可於全天任何時間點訂購，包括果汁、蛋、鬆餅、肉類、玉米粥，以及多種鬆餅特製品，如肉汁與鬆餅、鄉村火腿與鬆餅。午餐與晚餐項目包括炸與烤雞、雞肉與餃子、肉排、鄉村炸牛排、豬排、魚、鄉村炸蝦、牛排、蔬菜盤、三明治與沙拉。本公司亦提供多人份的外帶家庭餐盒。此外，有時會推出新項目作為非正式菜單特供或在特定店鋪試營運菜單，以評估提升顧客興趣的方式，並識別未來可能加入菜單的項目。本公司提供週間午餐特供，包含部分最受歡迎的主菜，以午餐份量提供。菜單亦包含週間與週末晚餐特供，展示熱門晚餐主菜。不同地區的菜單價格與內容略有差異。2025 年每位顧客平均消費為 15.23 美元，較前一年成長 6.8%。2025 年，典型店鋪每週平均服務約 5,330 名餐廳顧客。

● 提升員工體驗：我們推出了新的員工價值主張，我們認為這將有助於更好的招募與留任，並推出了技術方案以改善店長的經營體驗。
paragraphs: 以下為管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析（"MD&A"），提供管理層認為與評估及瞭解本公司合併營運成果與財務狀況相關之資訊。MD&A 應與合併財務報表及其附註一併閱讀。讀者亦應謹慎審閱本報告中 "風險因素" 節及其它警示聲明所載資訊。本 MD&A 中所報導或討論之所有金額（每股金額除外）均以千美元為單位表示。本 MD&A 中提及之年份或季度，除非特別說明或上下文清楚顯示否則均指本公司會計年度或會計季。
此摘要總結 MD&A，包含以下各節：
● 管理層總覽 – 本公司業務之一般說明、餐飲與零售產業、本公司戰略優先事項及關鍵績效指標。
● 營運成果 – 分析本公司合併營業收入陳述書，內容載於本公司合併財務報表中。
● 流動性與資本資源 – 分析本公司主要流動性來源、資本支出及重大承諾。
● 關鍵會計估計 – 討論需要關鍵判斷與估計之會計政策。

以下 MD&A 包含 2025 年與 2024 年項目之討論，以及 2025 年 8 月 1 日結業與 2024 年 8 月 2 日結業之間年度比較。未包含於本 MD&A 之中 2023 年項目及 2024 年 8 月 2 日結業與 2023 年 7 月 28 日結業之間年度比較資訊，可於本公司 2024 年 8 月 2 日結業年度 10-K 報告 "第二部分，第 7 項 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之分析" 中找到，該報告已於 2024 年 9 月 27 日向 SEC 提交。

Cracker Barrel Old Country Store, Inc.（"本公司"、"本公司" 或 "我們"）為一家公開上市公司（Nasdaq: CBRL），透過其營運及特定子公司之營運，主要從事 Cracker Barrel Old Country Store®（"Cracker Barrel"）概念之經營與發展。每間 Cracker Barrel 店鋪均為包含禮品店之餐廳。餐廳提供早餐、午餐與晚餐。禮品店提供多種裝飾與實用商品，專門銷售搖椅、節日禮物、玩具、服飾與食品。截至 2025 年 9 月 12 日，本公司經營 657 間 Cracker Barrel 店鋪，分佈於 43 個州。本公司亦擁有 Maple Street Biscuit Company（"MSBC"），為一家早餐與午餐快速餐飲概念。截至 2025 年 9 月 12 日，本公司經營 68 間 MSBC 分店，分佈於 10 個州。
本公司認為 Cracker Barrel 品牌仍是餐飲業中最具競爭力且差異化最高的品牌之一，並計畫持續運用並強化此品牌作為本公司業務策略的核心競爭零組件。我們的長期策略以三個主要業務要務為基礎：推動相關性、提供顧客喜愛的餐點與體驗，以及提升獲利能力。
本公司認為未來幾個季度總體經濟展望面臨重大挑戰，包括通貨膨脹與利率的持續波動、消費者負債水準提高與儲蓄率下降，以及地緣政治環境與全球貿易等其他因素所帶來的潛在不確定性。然而，儘管有這些挑戰，本公司仍專注於為股東帶來長期成長與回報。
2024 年，本公司宣佈了我們的多年度戰略計畫。此多年度戰略計畫建立在五項支柱之上，並在 2025 年逐步落實。這五項支柱如下：
● 品牌重塑：本公司建立了以「鄉村款待的善良」為核心的更新品牌識別，此識別已應用於行銷、產品（餐點與零售）以及實體內容與資產。本公司也優化了合作夥伴策略 – 例如與 NASCAR 合作 – 並擴展了其他行銷通路的使用。
● 提升商店與顧客體驗：本公司改善了多項營運速度指標，並導入新的分配軟體套件以提升零售產品管理。此外，本公司測試了多種零售店面佈局與商店翻修方案，以提升顧客的瀏覽與購物體驗。根據此測試所收集的顧客意見，翻修計畫已暫停執行。
● 在數位與外帶業務中取得優勢：本公司進一步運用忠誠度計畫，透過先進技術提供個別顧客的優惠，並優化與擴展外帶業務，透過更新節日與婚宴服務方案，並改善第三方銷售策略。

headings: 與總體經濟及產業條件相關的風險
購入價格波動及通貨膨脹情況可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務表現產生不利影響，而我們為抵銷或緩解這些情況所採取的措施可能不會有效。
與我們業務相關的風險
未能達成或維持我們多年戰略計畫的目標或結果，可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
我們面臨激烈的競爭，若我們無法持續有效地競爭，可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生不利影響。
未能最大化或成功主張我們的智慧財產權權利，可能對我們的業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
與我們資本結構相關的風險
2026 年票據或 2030 年票據的抵押契約中所規定的條款，可能延遲或阻卻對我們的收購。
與 2030 年票據相關的限額認購合約可能影響本公司普通股的價值。
與 2026 年可轉換票據的認購權證及選擇權交易可能影響本公司普通股的價值。
本公司對於可轉換票據認購權證交易及限額認購合約交易涉及交易對手風險。
與供應鏈相關的風險
本公司對某些重要供應商的依賴，特別是針對外來零售產品，可能使本公司面臨風險，這些風險可能對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
本公司管理零售存貨水準及商品組合變動的能力，可能對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
與資訊系統、網路安全及資料隱私相關的風險
本公司資訊科技、網路基礎建設及電信系統的重大中斷，可能對本公司業務、營運結果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
若我們或我們的供應商未能遵守隱私權及資料保護法規，或我們的系統遭入侵，將可能對我們的營運造成負面影響，且我們可能面臨訴訟及不利的公眾聲譽。
法律與法規風險
訴訟可能對我們的業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成負面影響。
我們的業務可能因激進股東的行動而受到負面影響。
我們章程中的條款、田納西州法律及我們股東權利協議的規定，可能阻卻潛在買家對本公司的收購。
與我們業務策略相關的風險
我們依賴吸引並留住合資格的員工，同時控制勞動成本。
關鍵高階主管的離職或在招募與留住合資格人員方面遇到困難，可能威脅我們未來的成長與成功。
本公司可能未來進行策略性投資或計畫，這些投資或計畫可能無法達到預期效益，導致部分或全部投資損失。
個別門市位置受當地條件影響，這些條件可能變化，並對這些門市的攜帶價值產生不利影響。
若未能充分處理永續性議題，可能對本公司品牌、業務、營運成果及財務狀況產生不利影響。
若本公司無法有效執行業務策略，包括尋找新門市位置並開設具盈利能力的新門市，本公司業務可能受影響。
paragraphs: 投資本公司證券涉及一定程度的風險。購買本公司證券之人士應謹慎考量下列所描述之風險，以及本年度報告表10-K及其他資訊，包含本公司合併財務報表及其附註。若任何下列風險實際發生，將可能對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果或現金流造成重大不利影響。在任何此類情況下，本公司證券之交易價格可能下跌，您可能損失全部或部分投資。

本公司營收與營運成果之強弱，取決於諸多因素，包括食品、原料、零售商品、運輸、配送、勞務及公用事業之價格與可得性。本公司已經驗過並持續經驗通貨膨脹壓力，針對這些成本。經濟條件波動、天氣、供應鏈中斷、運輸效率、需求及其他因素，也會影響本公司所購買之原料與零售商品之可得性、品質與成本。全球對玉米、小麥及乳製品之需求變化，已導致並可能繼續導致雞禽與畜牧業之飼料成本波動。本公司餐廳之營運毛利，受食品原料價格與可得性之影響，包括牛肉、豬肉、雞肉、乳製品與農產品。進口零售商品或食品商品之關稅或匯率變動，可能增加本公司成本，並可能影響這些商品之供應。

此外，本公司零售商品之價格亦同樣受經濟與通貨膨脹壓力影響，已導致並可能繼續導致成本上升與毛利率下降。本公司試圖透過提高餐點價格與營運改善來抵銷成本壓力，但可能無法成功。本公司致力於提供中等價格之產品，因此，本公司可能無法或無法完全將價格上漲轉嫁給客戶，以抵銷成本上漲，而不會對客戶需求造成不利影響。消費者可能較不願意支付本公司餐點價格，並可能 increasingly 前往價格較低之競爭對手，或限制其餐廳或零售商品之購買。價格上漲若無法足夠且及時抵銷更高成本，或導致營收數量顯著下降，可能對本公司營收與營運成果造成重大不利影響。
勞務是本公司營運成本之主要零組件，因最低工資提高、競爭、失業率或醫療與其他福利成本增加所導致之勞務成本上升，可能對本公司營運成果造成重大不利影響。本公司在許多州與地方運營，這些地方之最低工資遠高於聯邦最低工資。本公司之經銷商與供應商也可能受更高最低工資、福利標準與合規成本影響，這可能導致供應給本公司之商品與服務成本上升。美國勞動市場競爭激烈，已導致工資上漲，未來可能持續如此。
本公司營運毛利亦受影響，無論是因總體經濟通貨膨脹或其他因素，皆因天然氣與電力等公用事業價格波動，而本公司各據點之大部分能源供應皆依賴這些公用事業。本公司未能有效預見並回應任何這些因素之一或數個不利變動，可能對本公司營運成果造成重大不利影響。通貨膨脹壓力及其他影響這些項目成本之變動，可能對本公司在2026年業務造成負面影響。
疫情、流行病、地方性傳染病及其他公共衛生問題，或政府對食品產品消費及廣泛傳染病之相關規範，可能減少消費者人流量，並可能對本公司業務、營運成果與財務狀況造成不利影響。
